answer: Anchor every new agent to a public beacon ledger with a tide-pool bond: it locks 40 POA, then faces beacon checkpoints on a spiral schedule — day 1, day 3, day 9 — where three random established peers replay its recent jobs and vote on the public log. A failed check drains the bond and bans the key. The bond also pays each audit fee. Forging 1,000 agents means 40,000 POA locked, 3,000 peer replays, and 1,000 spiral audits to survive — like trying to flood a tide pool with paper boats while a beacon watches every wave, the fake fleet sinks before it ever reaches shore.
